messages:
olivia: Heads-up — CI is intermittently failing when publishing the infra-builder image to eu-west-1/us-west-2. Observed terraform plan in Dedicated accounts showing image tag drift (same tag -> different digest). Anyone seen this before? :grimacing:

sam: saw one alert this morning about immutable-tag mismatch. Can you paste the publish log?

olivia: here are the relevant bits from the build job output:
```
# buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --tag registry.redwood-infra/dev/infra-builder:ci-20260310 \
  --push .
Pushing manifest for registry.redwood-infra/dev/infra-builder:ci-20260310
... OK
Digest: sha256:abc123... (eu-west-1)
Digest: sha256:def456... (us-west-2)
```
The job reports success but the digests differ across regions right after push. Terraform picks the registered digest in eu-west, but the private cluster in us-west resolves to a different digest and that causes cluster to re-pull/recreate nodes.

ci-bot: build-7883 failed to reconcile manifest on second registry endpoint (rate-limited retry). See job: https://ci.redwood/7883

maria: probable cause: our multi-arch manifest push is non-atomic across our registries/replicas. If we push to a global registry fronted by regional mirrors, the mirrors can present different digests until propagation finishes. Also if we re-tag and re-push quickly, some regions will see the new blob but others still point at the old.

jamal: +1. Another angle: we used build cache that included local layers with different timestamps, so the layer digests could legitimately differ between builders if we inadvertently used non-deterministic metadata. Were build args or timestamps injected?

olivia: we do set BUILD_DATE and GIT_COMMIT in labels. But the same CI job for both arches should produce identical layer digests if everything is deterministic. Not sure why the registry is returning two digests for the same tag.

sam: quick mitigation: don't let Terraform use mutable tags. Pin to manifest digest in images.yaml when we sync infra. Also make the publish step push a digest-only reference and record it as an artifact in CI. That way terraform uses a digest like registry/...@sha256:xxx.

maria: agree. Also we should decouple SBOM/signing from the push path: generate SBOM and cosign it as a separate artifact so mirrors can't lag the signature. And make the release job upload both: manifest/digest + SBOM + signature.

jamal: implementation notes — use buildx with --provenance and --sbom flags, then run `docker buildx imagetools inspect` to capture the final manifest digest. Example snippet we can add to the pipeline:
```
# build & push
docker buildx build --platform=linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --push \
  --label org.opencontainers.image.revision=$GIT_SHA \
  --label org.opencontainers.image.created=$BUILD_DATE \
  -t $REG/$REPO:$TAG .
# capture manifest digest
DIGEST=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect $REG/$REPO:$TAG -f '{{index .Manifests 0 "Digest"}}')
echo "artifact_digest=$DIGEST" > artifact.properties
```
Note: the templating depends on version, but CI can parse the `imagetools inspect` JSON.

infra-bot: registry quotas: pushing every CI run to the global registry is hitting mirror sync windows + our rate limits. Consider using a promotion model: push to a staging repo (us-west primary) then replicate, or use signed immutable releases for promoted builds.

olivia: proposal for next steps:
- stop referencing mutable tags in infra manifests; require digest pinning for dedicated + production clusters (short-term change)
- update CI: after push, capture manifest digest and write to a single artifacts bucket + release note, and upload SBOM + cosign signature
- add a CI gating test that pulls the pushed tag from multiple regions and verifies the manifest digest is identical across endpoints before we write the artifact properties
- add a GitOps pre-sync check that refuses to apply a mutable tag (fail early)

sam: I can open an RFC and a GH issue for the CI change. Also suggest adding `--cache-from` with a registry cache to make builds deterministic and speed them up. Might reduce variations in layers.

maria: can also add a lightweight integration test in the staging rollout: after GitOps applies the new image-digest, run a smoke deploy to a canary host and assert container image digest matches the pinned digest. If mismatch -> rollback.

jamal: timeline: I can prototype the cross-region digest check this week. If we add that to the publish job, we can gate promotion to production until parity is confirmed.

olivia: awesome. sam — can you include SBOM and cosign steps in the RFC? One thing to decide: where do we store the SBOM artifact canonical location? artifact-bucket vs registry artifact store?

sam: leaning artifact-bucket (S3) with strong immutability + lifecycle policy. Registry stores can be flaky across mirrors. We should store metadata in a single source-of-truth (artifact-bucket) and link the digest -> SBOM -> signature.

infra-bot: note — we need to check KMS permissions for cosign in ephemeral CI runners. Some runners don't have access to production KMS keys; consider short-lived keywrap tokens or a signing service.

maria: good catch. We can prototype using an ephemeral key per CI job and back it with an HSM wrap key for prod promotions.

olivia: ok plan looks good. Action items: sam open RFC + GH issue for CI + SBOM, jamal protos cross-region digest check, I'll file a follow-up to require digest pinning in terraform module and add migration notes for teams.

sam: will do. tagging in the issue: @oncall @security for cosign/KMS review.

jamal: and add a CI test to ensure `docker manifest inspect` returns same digest across our mirror endpoints. If not, fail and alert infra oncall.

olivia: thanks everyone — I'll update the infra channel once RFC is up. :rocket:

sam: thanks :thumbsup:
